title: GC-STEM SCB and CDE Manifest
description: Version 3.0 structural contract for the shared STEM Computing Baseline (SCB) in atlas/.config/scb_manifest.json and the required .config/cde_manifest.json in every STEM course repository. The SCB establishes common capabilities, supported component requirements, sources, platforms, workflows, settings, and assets. Each CDE manifest identifies its course and explicitly declares additions, or an empty additions object. All courses consume the selected local Atlas checkout; no per-course baseline snapshot, exact SCB release, checksum pin, or identical software version across platforms is required. An IDE is a concrete software product within the complete CDE.
$comment: Composition and environment verification are automation responsibilities, not JSON Schema merge features. Canonical ownership: GC-STEM/.github owns schemas/manifest.schema.json; GC-STEM/atlas owns .config/scb_manifest.json and shared automation; each course owns its required .config/cde_manifest.json. Resolve ATLAS_ROOT from the selected Atlas checkout and COURSE_ROOT from the selected course checkout, rather than assuming clone directory names or the process working directory. Required resolver order: (1) Require and read the course manifest and ${ATLAS_ROOT}/.config/scb_manifest.json without executing manifest content; reject duplicate JSON keys. A missing CDE file is an error, including for SCB-only courses. (2) Validate both inputs, schema support, baseline identity, approval state, and release provenance using policy supplied by the approved automation. A self-declared approved status alone does not establish trust. Baseline versions are release/reporting metadata, not equality gates; do not require identical baseline bytes or product versions across courses, platforms, or students, and do not fetch, update, or switch Atlas merely to validate a course. (3) Deep-copy the SCB configuration catalogs, policy, and logging. Add course catalog entries by stable ID, then apply platform_extensions to baseline or newly added platforms. Existing IDs are conflicts, including identical repeated entries. Arrays in newly added or replaced objects are atomic values, not append/union operations. (4) For each override, require a named baseline permission with exactly the same target, a matching course allowlist if present, and an existing baseline target. Reject duplicate or ancestor/descendant override targets, missing targets, additions overlapping a replaced object, and attempts to override metadata or permissions. Replace the complete target object. A course cannot authorize its own exceptions. (5) Assemble the resolved CDE with course identity/control, baseline reference, baseline_release/baseline_control, the SCB automation release, and course-owned environment declarations; use an empty environment map when none are declared. Validate #/$defs/resolvedConfiguration. Record the exact Atlas release/revision and actual component versions used for troubleshooting without treating those recorded values as course pins. (6) Before any changing action, validate referenced products, capabilities, sources, retries, providers, settings, environments, platforms, deployments, workflows, and adapters; validate source integrity, calendar dates, compatible component requirements, duplicate/conflicting settings and asset destinations, approved path boundaries, obsolete-component safety, and secrets/personal values. Verify required capabilities and applicable component version rules, not equality with a reference machine. Preserve compatible installations; install missing requirements, repair unmet requirements, and never downgrade automatically solely to match the reference platform. managed_latest permits refreshing approved software only during an explicitly selected update action; verification must not demand that every installation be the newest release. (7) Resolve each course environment beneath COURSE_ROOT and confirm its runtime capability/binding. Environment-bound packages must be installed and verified with that environment's own interpreter/package manager, never global pip or another course's environment. Two course checkouts must not resolve to the same managed environment directory. (8) Validate deployment releases, architectures, roles, states, action order, update mode, workflow authorizations, success transitions, exactly one enabled reference platform, and exactly one enabled reference deployment linked to it. Reference environments are qualification examples, not requirements to reproduce identical machines. Unresolved conflicts are fatal; never use file order or last-writer-wins. Structural validation cannot compare files, resolve dynamic IDs, prove authorization/integrity, verify installed tools, or implement these semantic checks.

$schema.description: Optional editor/validator association with the shared GC-STEM schema. This reference validates structure; it does not load or merge the SCB manifest.

scbManifest.description: Shared SCB stored only in the selected Atlas checkout at .config/scb_manifest.json. It has no course identity or parent baseline. Its data selects common capabilities and compatible component requirements, without imposing identical machine versions.

$schema.description: Optional editor/validator association with the shared GC-STEM schema. This reference validates structure; it does not load or merge the SCB manifest.

courseManifest.description: Required .config/cde_manifest.json in every STEM course repository. Set additions to {} and overrides to [] when the course uses only the SCB. Course-owned environments are optional and declared only when required by this course. JSON Schema defaults do not supply data.

resolvedConfiguration.description: In-memory complete CDE produced by the approved resolver. Validate explicitly against #/$defs/resolvedConfiguration before changing the environment. This is not a third input manifest or required repository file. control is the course record; baseline_control and baseline_release record the shared SCB actually read. The SCB supplies automation_release and its date-time group. Course environments come from the course manifest or an empty map. Recorded releases support diagnostics and do not impose equality or per-course SCB pins.

baselineIdentity.description: Identity and release metadata of the common SCB. version is independent of schema_version and automation_release and is recorded for support; courses do not have to pin this version.

path.description: Shared SCB in the selected local Atlas checkout. Resolve ATLAS_ROOT from setup configuration or the selected checkout, not from a guessed home/sibling path. Validation does not fetch or update Atlas.

baselineReference.description: Shared Atlas SCB dependency for every course. No per-course SCB copy, exact baseline version, or file digest is required. Component-specific requirements are expressed with version rules in the relevant products/bindings, not baseline equality constraints.

environment_name.description: Name of this course's complete Course Development Environment (CDE), including the SCB and any course-specific requirements.

repository_name.description: Course repository name, without an owner, .git suffix, or directory path. Exposed to approved path templates as ${COURSE_REPOSITORY}. A student's clone may use a different directory name; COURSE_ROOT is resolved at runtime.

course.description: Course identity belongs in each course's .config/cde_manifest.json, never in the reusable SCB.

courseId.description: Institutional course identifier. No STEM subject prefix, course number range, or course title is hard-coded in the schema.

courseAdditions.description: Required object of new course catalog entries and platform package/binding additions. {} explicitly means no additions. Individual sections must be nonempty when present. Catalogs are maps keyed by stable IDs, not arrays. Existing IDs, duplicate managed-setting destinations/keys, and conflicting assets are errors; there is no last-writer-wins merge.

platformExtension.description: Add new OS support package IDs or capability binding IDs to an existing baseline or newly added platform. An existing nested ID is a conflict even if the repeated value is identical. Use an authorized explicit override to replace an existing baseline entry.

overridePermissions.description: Baseline-owned permissions for explicit course overrides. An empty object permits no overrides. These permissions must come from a trusted, approved SCB release, not merely a locally edited baseline that passes structural validation.

allowed_course_ids.description: Optional course allowlist. If omitted, the permission applies to any course consuming this approved baseline permission. Course IDs are matched exactly, including punctuation/case.

overridePermission.description: Permission owned by the SCB. A course cannot create permissions. Semantic validation requires an existing baseline target and at most one permission per target. Replacement values still must satisfy this schema and all approved release constraints.

value.description: Complete replacement object. The target-specific branch validates its exact shape.

override.description: Explicit complete-entry replacement authorized by the named baseline permission. Runtime checks must confirm exact target equality, course eligibility, a pre-existing baseline target, unique non-overlapping targets, and a valid final CDE.

overrideTarget.description: Exact JSON Pointer to an existing baseline catalog entry, platform package/binding, policy object, or logging object. Wildcards, array indexes, arbitrary leaf edits, metadata changes, and permission changes are unsupported. Replacement values are complete objects, not patches.

adapterId.description: Identifier for reviewed executable behavior distributed with the package. Manifest data may select but not define adapters.

schemaVersion.description: Version 3.0 is a breaking replacement for the version 2.x single-course contract.

pathTemplate.description: Portable path template using variables permitted by policy.allowed_path_variables: ${HOME}, ${DESKTOP}, ${COURSE_REPOSITORY}, ${ATLAS_ROOT}, ${COURSE_ROOT}, ${SCRIPT_ROOT}, ${LOG_DIR}, and ${TEMP}. Resolve Atlas/course roots from actual selected checkouts. Semantic validation rejects unknown placeholders, expands approved variables, canonicalizes results, and confirms approved boundaries.

versionRule.description: Requirement for an individual component, not a requirement for version equality across courses or platforms. presence_only accepts a usable installed implementation; minimum and compatible_range accept any supported version satisfying that rule. exact is reserved for a documented component-specific need. Preserve an installed version that satisfies the applicable requirement. managed_latest selects approved versions during an explicit update action and does not make newer availability a verification failure.

executable_names.description: Candidate command names for locating the product. A runtime adapter may select one suitable interpreter; it must not require every platform-specific alias to exist.

verification.description: Evidence interpreted by the selected adapter. For programming runtimes, discover a usable interpreter and verify its applicable component version rule before falling back to package registration checks. A compatible approved runtime need not have the exact package identifier used by the installation recipe. Required product identity, functionality, integrity, and applicable settings checks still apply.

course_root.description: Portable discovery/default template for the course checkout. COURSE_ROOT must use the actual selected clone location; repository_name does not force a directory name or path.

script_root.description: Shared automation directory in the selected Atlas checkout, not a duplicated course script tree. Resolve ATLAS_ROOT before expanding this path.

version_management.description: Establish common usable capabilities. Satisfying installations are preserved; normal setup does not force newest versions or match a reference machine. Install missing components and repair unmet requirements. A conflict requiring downgrade or replacement must be reported for explicit resolution, not silently applied.

implementation_kind.description: Kind of software implementing this capability. ide and ide_extension refer to actual IDE products and their extensions, such as PyCharm or Visual Studio; they do not name the whole CDE.

capabilityCatalog.description: SCB or resolved capability catalog. Each capability declares whether it is required. No language, IDE, testing tool, or programming-course capability is mandatory merely because of this schema.

product_kind.description: Kind of the concrete product. Preserve IDE terminology for an actual IDE product or extension; CDE names the complete course environment.

source_type.description: Distribution channel for concrete products. ide_marketplace refers to a particular IDE's extension marketplace.

providerProfileCatalog.description: Service provider profiles. This catalog may be empty when no selected product needs an external provider.

osPackage.description: Platform support package that is not itself a Course Development Environment capability. Course Development Environment products must be represented under cde_bindings.

environment_id.description: ID in the course-owned environment catalog; required exactly for course_environment scope. Semantic validation resolves it before install or verification.

cdeBinding.description: Platform-specific product implementation of a capability. Compatible installed versions may differ across platforms. package_identifier selects the installation recipe when installation is needed; it does not require replacing an already approved compatible runtime distributed under another package identifier. course_environment targets a declared per-course environment; python_venv_package requires that scope and must install/verify with the named virtual environment's interpreter instead of global pip.

cdeBindings.description: Concrete product bindings for capabilities in a Course Development Environment (CDE). Keep operating-system support packages in os_packages. Semantic validation checks required capabilities against the final enabled platform and deployment configuration.

reference_platform.description: True for the platform implementation containing the approved reference deployment profile. Exactly one enabled reference platform is required in each complete SCB or resolved configuration.

os_packages.description: Operating-system-specific prerequisites and support utilities. Do not list official Course Development Environment products here.

reference_profile.description: True only for the approved environment used for primary development, documentation, support reproduction, and acceptance testing.

platform_id.description: Identifier of the platform implementation used by this deployment.

allowed_workflow_ids.description: Lifecycle workflow identifiers authorized for this deployment profile.

deploymentProfile.description: A concrete environment in which a platform implementation is deployed. Deployment profiles keep provider, desktop-environment, session, reset, release, architecture, and authorized workflow details separate from software and package bindings.

deploymentProfileCatalog.description: Catalog of local, virtual, hosted, or other deployment environments. Semantic validation requires exactly one enabled reference profile and validates every allowed workflow reference.

starting_state_id.description: Course-independent starting state. course_master replaces the legacy course-specific state name.

lifecycleWorkflow.description: Declarative, non-executable lifecycle sequence selected from deployment profile, operating role, and starting state. Applies to any STEM course.

lifecycleWorkflowCatalog.description: Controlled workflow catalog. Semantic validation confirms ordered actions and success transitions agree and that each workflow is authorized by every referenced deployment profile.

values.description: Concrete product-specific settings. Keys and values are validated by the selected settings adapter.

versionDateTimeGroup.description: Local version date-time group in YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM format using a 24-hour clock. Semantic validation must confirm that the calendar date is valid.

semanticVersion.description: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version with optional pre-release and build metadata.

courseEnvironmentCatalog.description: Optional course-owned environments keyed by stable ID. Omit or use {} when none are needed. These declarations do not add capabilities or install packages by themselves; environment-bound platform bindings name an environment_id.

path.description: Course-local environment directory. Resolve and canonicalize beneath the actual COURSE_ROOT; reject aliases/symlinks escaping that boundary or sharing another course's environment.

courseEnvironment.description: An isolated Python virtual environment owned by this course. Use a supported interpreter implementing runtime_capability_id and install/verify packages inside this environment. Its packages may differ from other courses without changing shared tools.
